# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

- VERIFIED (cand_0001, +0.375): stating that the grader reads `data_only=True` without recalc, so values must be written as literals and never as formulas, plus a reload-and-verify step, fixed 16 tasks.
- VERIFIED by simulation (cand_0002 diagnosis): openpyxl save drops cached formula values inside the answer range (267-18). `ws.max_row` overcounts because of blank rows (80-42). Float `>=` thresholds need an epsilon (51-12). The preview's "Unnamed" headers mean the header is not in Excel row 1 (59196). Column mapping by position read the answer column (2768).

## Rules the reader reads but skips (from the cand_0002 traces, diagnosed in cand_0003)
- What didn't work (confirmed by cand_0002 RESULT broke={48527, 37456} and the 2768/50768/43436 persisting): one-line advisory rules ("check your rule reproduces every example", "locate columns by header text", "axis labels decide", "prefer the point-in-time header") were present in the prompt and skipped by the reader whenever the instruction prose pointed elsewhere.
- Promising (cand_0003, pending RESULT): turn each one into a precondition with a printout (`cell, existing, yours`), a copyable idiom (`dict(zip(hdr,row))`), or a precise discriminator (where the axis title sits; "a diagonal example can't confirm orientation").
